observations: body L1: the sentence begun on p. 244 goes on: «in fragmento chronologico Heraclii imperatoris».

body L4, L21, L23-L25, L29, L34-L36: the dashes of «Al–Battānī», «al–Bīrūnī», «al–Battānī», «al–Ǵīlī», «al–Khāzinī», «az–», «–zīǵ», «al–Kharaqī», «’l–faẓl», «Āyīn–i–Akbarī», «’l–qarnayn», «al–» and «–Battānī» are long dashes (4.0 to 6.1 pt); the dash after «az» at the end of L24 is repeated at the beginning of L25, and that after «al» at the end of L34 at the beginning of L35, as printed. The hyphen of «as-sanǵarī» measures 2.6 pt; «al–Battānī» in L23 is not letter-spaced.

body L8-L14: the dates are right: with 1 tūt on 29 August Julian (30 August in the year before a Julian leap year) and the Gregorian calendar 13 days ahead of the Julian (note 1), 1 tūt falls on 11 September (12 September in the Coptic intercalary years), and each month of 30 days gives 11 October, 10 November, 10 December, 9 January and 8 February (one day later in those years); 1 barmahāt falls on 10 March in both, since the Gregorian February after an intercalary Coptic year has 29 days. The signs of equality measure 9.4 to 9.7 pt and the guillemets are ditto marks. The months are spelled «bābeh» and «hatūr» here (p. 243: bābah, hatūr).
body L10-L11, L13: specks after the sign of equality of «hatūr», after the 11 of «11 Dec.» and over the m of «amshīr» are not transcribed.
body L15, L32, L34: the dashes of «282–283» and «18–23» are long dashes (5.5 and 5.4 pt); in the head the dash after «c)» measures 9.2 pt, the dash after «incidat.» 9.8 pt.

body L24-L28: 13 November 30 B.C. (proleptic Julian calendar) was a Thursday, and from it to the epoch of Yazdegerd, 16 June 632, are 241281 days, Ibn Yūnus' number (note 3); 31 August 30 B.C. was a Sunday.
body L29: «vers» has no period, and the sign of equality measures 9.7 pt; kept as printed.
body L27: the o of «Ptolemaei» prints broken.
notes_left L1-L3: the hyphens at the ends of «Fe-», «ca-» and «praece-» print as raised dots.
notes_left L4-L5: the dash after «dit.» measures 9.0 pt; 29 August 284 (Julian calendar) was a Friday.
notes_right L1-L2: the dash after «632-633.» measures 8.3 pt and the hyphens of «632-633», «1009-1010» and «83-84» 2.3 to 3.0 pt; the year 400 of the Hijra runs from 25 August 1009 to 14 August 1010.
notes_right L5: «pag» has no period before the comma; kept as printed.
